source_caption:
Vigilante — Justice Outside the Law

Vigilante follows a man who becomes determined to confront criminals who continue to escape meaningful consequences through the legal system. Frustrated by the gap between justice and punishment, he begins taking matters into his own hands.

As his actions become more extreme, he finds himself caught between his desire to protect innocent people and the consequences of operating outside the law. Each confrontation forces him to question how far he is willing to go in the name of justice.

The story explores themes of revenge, morality, justice, corruption, and personal responsibility. It raises the question of whether someone can truly deliver justice without becoming part of the violence they are fighting against.

What makes Vigilante compelling is the tension between doing what feels right and following the law. Every decision carries consequences, making the line between hero and criminal increasingly difficult to define.

💬 When the law can't protect everyone, who decides what justice looks like?

source_details.synopsis: The Vigilante, marketed as The Vigilante: Fighting Hero of the West, is a 1947 American Western film serial directed by Wallace Fox. The 33rd serial released by Columbia Pictures, it was based on the comic book cowboy Vigilante, who first appeared in Action Comics, published by DC Comics. It stars Ralph Byrd, well known for his central role in the Dick Tracy serials. It was his last serial appearance.
